name: Avenue Supermarts Ltd
about: Avenue Supermarts Limited (DMart) is a national supermarket chain, with a focus on value-retailing. We offer a wide range of products with a focus on the Foods, Non-Foods (FMCG) and General Merchandise & Apparel product categories. [1]

statements.text: Revenue compounded 23.3% a year over 5 years (FY21→FY26); profit after tax 22.0%.
EBITDA margin held roughly flat over 5 years (7.2% → 7.5%).
Revenue growth accelerated from 13% to 18% YoY over the last 4 quarters.
Over 5 years: ₹12,083 cr of profit, ₹12,678 cr of operating cash — conversion 1.05x.

ledger.quote: we should be opening around 15% of our store base as the number that we want to increase annually.
ledger.statement: Store additions of around 15% of the store base each year (internal benchmark)
ledger.speaker: Anshul Asawa
ledger.evidence: There is no store count in the inputs. In Q1 FY25 an analyst said additions had been 'trending below the 15% number' for several years, with FY25 expected at 40-45 stores (C5, C6), and the same benchmark was restated in Q1 FY27 without a dated commitment. It also conflicts with the '40, 40, 40' guide (G7).

ledger.quote: 15% kind of a gross margin and let's say around a 5% kind of a net margin should be the North Star for this business even in the future.
ledger.statement: Gross margin around 15% and net margin around 5% as long-term north star
ledger.speaker: Anshul Asawa
ledger.evidence: Gross margin is not in the inputs. Net margin was 4.8% in FY26 per management (C1, likely standalone), while TTM consolidated PAT of INR 3,115 crore on INR 74,224 crore revenue is about 4.2% (F:ttm_pat_cr, F:ttm_revenue_cr). Both are below the 5% marker, but it is a long-term 'North Star' with no date.
ledger.actual_text: Net margin 4.8% FY26 standalone (C1); about 4.2% TTM consolidated

ledger.quote: we might go to an INR2,000 crores borrowing by the end of the year
ledger.statement: Possible INR2,000 crore borrowing by end of FY27 to fund capex
ledger.speaker: Niladri Deb
ledger.evidence: FY27 has not ended. Net borrowing was about INR 965 crore and total debt including Ind AS 116 leases INR 2,267 crore at March 2026 (C1). The facts show borrowings of INR 4,264 crore (F:borrowings_cr) on an unstated date and basis. If that is like-for-like with the INR 2,267 crore, debt has already risen by about INR 2,000 crore, and it is unclear whether INR 2,000 crore is the total or the increment.

ledger.quote: We should deliver everything within six hours.
ledger.statement: Target to deliver all DMart Ready online orders within six hours
ledger.speaker: Neville Noronha
ledger.evidence: No delivery-time or fulfilment data is in the inputs. The only e-commerce datapoints are 17% sales growth and an INR 307 crore loss (C2).

ledger.quote: A broad trend line will be around the current run rates of around 23%
ledger.statement: General merchandise and apparel (GMA) share trend line of around 23%
ledger.speaker: Neville Noronha
ledger.evidence: No category mix is reported after the Q1 FY25 call, so the 23% GMA trend line cannot be tracked.

ledger.quote: typically 10% to 15% of my number count should be my new store opening, broadly
ledger.statement: New store openings of about 10-15% of the existing store count each year
ledger.speaker: Neville Noronha
ledger.evidence: There is no store count in the inputs. The Q1 FY25 analyst exchange (C5, C6) says additions were running below the top of this 10-15% range, but gives no figure for FY25-FY27.

ledger.speaker: Neville Noronha
ledger.evidence: There is no store count in the inputs. A flat 40 stores a year means a falling percentage growth rate as the base grows, which contradicts the 10-15% (G6) and 15% (G1) benchmarks.

ledger.quote: whatever we do today, 14%-15% gross margin, we're going to play around that
ledger.statement: Gross margin to stay in a 14-15% range
ledger.speaker: Neville Noronha
ledger.evidence: Gross margin is not in the facts. The operating margin has fallen 100 bps over three years (F:margin_change_3y_bps) and was 7.1% in Q2 FY27 against 7.3% a year earlier, which a flat gross margin would only explain if operating costs rose.

ledger.quote: The theme is the same, 15%, 20%. Okay? You replace everything that I said, 15% with 20% even for this year, right? That's the aspiration.
ledger.statement: Aspirational 15-20% CAGR growth, with store addition as the driver
ledger.speaker: Neville Noronha
ledger.evidence: No horizon. Three-year revenue CAGR is 17.1% (F:rev_cagr_3y), and quarterly YoY growth over the last four quarters was 13.3%, 18.9%, 14.9% and 17.8% (F:rev_yoy_last4_pct), inside the 15-20% aspiration on average. FY26 revenue per sq ft was flat and like-for-like growth was 8.1% (C1), so roughly half the growth comes from new space.

tones.label: cautious
tones.why: Management gives a store-addition benchmark but calls the 15% figure approximate and avoids firm growth numbers.

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Management is very bullish on store acceleration and online delivery, though it gives few numeric targets.

tones.label: cautious
tones.why: Management says it will not give forward-looking numbers, tempers expectations on GMA share and gross margin, and calls even a 15% CAGR aspiration dependent on store additions.

context.speaker: Niladri Deb
context.text: Hello, everyone. Good morning to you. So I'm referring to slide number 10, where we see bill cuts. We have a healthy growth reaching close to 40 crore bill cuts in the year gone by. Our like- for-like store growth, which is stores more than two years old, grew about 8.1% for the last year. At the end of March 2026, we had about 20.6 million square feet of retail business area, and our revenue per square foot from all stores put together came in about flat at INR33,422 per square foot. Moving to slide 11. We reported a turnover of close to INR67,000 crores in the year gone by. EBITDA margin came in at about 7.8%. Profit after tax was about 4.8%, INR3,224 crores of profit, and we generated INR4,168 crores of cash from the operations. The inventory days went up to 33.2. This is also due to more warehouses that we opened during the year so that we could better service our customers. Days payables remained flat at 7.2, continuing our strategy of paying vendors quickly. Total Debt inched up slightly to INR2,267 crores. This INR2,267 crores also includes debt arising out of AS 116 adjustment. The actual debt, which is net borrowing on the company, is close to INR965 crores as of March 2026 end. Fixed asset turnover came in at about 3.2 times, and the inventory turnover came at 12.8, which is an outcome of the higher number of inventory days that we're holding, leading to return on net worth coming at about 13.5% during the year and ROCE at about 17.1%, which are slightly lower than what we reported the prior year. Slide number 13 shows us the split of standalone and consolidated financials for March 2026 year gone by. Sales grew by close to 16%. Gross margin expanded by 16 bps. context.speaker: Anshul Asawa
context.text: Thank you, Aditya. Thanks for your questions. So let me take them one by one. Your first question, which is on exclusive brands and private label. I think our strategy or approach has not changed. You know, in the past we have spoken about the 20-20-20 principle. And I think my own personal reflection is that, you know, also given my previous background, that Indian market is still a very brand-conscious market. And so therefore, for any retailer to succeed in this, you know, you need to deliver real value to customers. Also, as you know, that we are an MRP-driven market, so therefore comparisons are very easy for people to make. And so therefore, you can only give real value when you are able to give, as per our 20-20-20 principle, you know, something where you can give at least a 20% price advantage. You should be able to make, some margin, which in our case we believe should be at least 20% more than the benchmark, and you should have a right to at least get 20% volume share, which basically means that we need to give true value, that's why customers would want to buy from us. And so therefore, wherever it makes sense for us, wherever we see that there is leverage that we can drive, we are participating and we are, driving that private label business. And we are talking here specifically about FMCG private label because as you possibly know that we do not count in that private label the numbers of our garments and general merchandise, or for that matter, DMart Grocery as well, which as you know, a lot of it sells as our own brand or private label. But coming back to the FMCG private label, so wherever we believe that we can give great value to customers while making, you know, reasonable margin, we would continue to drive that. business.what_it_does: Indian value retailer operating DMart stores selling grocery/FMCG, general merchandise and apparel. It had 20.6 million sq ft of retail area at March 2026, revenue per sq ft of INR 33,422 (about flat) and FY26 turnover of about INR 67,000 crore. Subsidiaries are Avenue E-commerce (DMart Ready online grocery), Align Retail (grocery packing) and Avenue Food Plaza (food counters beside stores).

segments.name: General merchandise and apparel (GMA)
segments.comment: Run-rate share of about 23% cited in the Q1 FY25 call as the trend line; no later figure is in the inputs. Apparel was then the fastest-growing category.

segments.name: Foods and FMCG (rest of store sales)
segments.comment: Not stated; about 77% is implied if GMA is 23%. FMCG private label is run on a '20-20-20' rule: at least 20% price advantage, 20% higher margin than the benchmark, and 20% volume share.

segments.name: Avenue E-commerce (DMart Ready)
segments.comment: FY26 sales +17%, EBITDA down 43%, net loss INR 307 crore.

segments.name: Align Retail and Avenue Food Plaza
segments.comment: Align Retail sales +16.5% and PAT +24%; Food Plaza sales +35.5% with a 9% PAT margin after a prior-year loss.

credibility.label: medium
credibility.summary: The 15-20% growth aspiration is being met: three-year revenue CAGR is 17.1% and Q2 FY27 grew 17.8%. But the store-opening benchmark keeps moving, from '10-15%' and 'about 40 a year' in Q1 FY25 to '15% of the base' in Q1 FY27, with analysts already flagging years of under-delivery. Profit has grown at less than half the revenue rate, and none of the store or gross-margin targets can be checked from reported data.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Aspiration of 15-20% growth driven by store additions (G9, G1).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Revenue CAGR is 17.1% over three years and 23.3% over five, and Q2 FY27 grew 17.8% YoY. FY26 like-for-like growth was 8.1% with revenue per sq ft flat at INR 33,422, so the rest of the growth came from new space.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: A net margin of about 5% is the 'North Star', and FY26 PAT was 4.8% (G2, C1).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: TTM PAT of INR 3,115 crore on INR 74,224 crore revenue is about 4.2%, and three-year PAT CAGR of 7.7% is less than half the 17.1% revenue CAGR. The operating margin is down 100 bps over three years, and Avenue E-commerce lost INR 307 crore in FY26.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Stores open at about 15% of the base each year (G1), alongside 10-15% (G6) and '40, 40, 40' (G7).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: In Q1 FY25 an analyst said additions had run below 15% for 'last few years', with FY25 tracking 40-45 stores, and that 55/65/75 a year would be needed for a 15% CAGR (C5, C6). A fixed 40 a year shrinks as a percentage of a growing base, so the three guides cannot all hold.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: The balance sheet stays conservative: net borrowing about INR 965 crore at March 2026, possibly rising to about INR 2,000 crore to fund capex (C1, G3).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: D/E is low at 0.16, but five-year FCF is INR -2,211 crore despite CFO/PAT of 1.05, so expansion capex has outrun internal cash. Reported borrowings are INR 4,264 crore, and inventory days rose to 33.2 with the cash cycle moving from 26 to 29 days.

bull.point: Growth is steady and in line with the stated aspiration: three-year revenue CAGR 17.1%, Q2 FY27 +17.8% YoY, TTM revenue INR 74,224 crore and FY26 like-for-like growth of 8.1%.

Cash conversion is real and leverage is low: FY26 operating cash flow was INR 4,168 crore against INR 3,224 crore PAT, five-year CFO/PAT is 1.05, D/E is 0.16, and vendors are paid in 7.2 days, so growth is not funded by suppliers.
Adjacencies are improving: Align Retail PAT +24% on sales +16.5%, and Avenue Food Plaza revenue +35.5% with a 9% PAT margin after a prior-year loss.

bear.point: Profit is lagging sales: three-year PAT CAGR is 7.7% against 17.1% for revenue, the operating margin is down 100 bps over three years, and Q2 FY27 margin was 7.1% against 7.3%. FY26 ROCE (17.1%) and RoNW (13.5%) were 'slightly lower'.

Expansion is consuming cash and debt is rising: five-year FCF is INR -2,211 crore, management flags borrowing of about INR 2,000 crore by FY27-end, and reported borrowings stand at INR 4,264 crore. Inventory days have risen to 33.2.

Online is a growing drain and the store yardstick is soft: Avenue E-commerce EBITDA fell 43% to an INR 307 crore loss, about 9.5% of FY26 PAT of INR 3,224 crore. The store-addition target has been stated as 15%, 10-15% and '40 a year'.

questions: How many stores did you add in FY26 and H1 FY27 as a percentage of the opening base? Which guide should investors hold you to: 15% of base, 10-15%, or about 40 a year?
Avenue E-commerce lost INR 307 crore in FY26 with EBITDA down 43% on 17% sales growth. What is the timeline to break-even, and what share of orders currently meets the six-hour delivery target?

Reported borrowings are INR 4,264 crore against INR 2,267 crore total debt (including leases) and INR 965 crore net at March 2026. What is net debt today, is the INR 2,000 crore FY27 figure the total or the increment, and where is gross margin against the 14-15% band?
